title: Weak homotopy equivalences glue over a binary open cover
statement: Use the continuous cubical homotopy groups and path components of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]: for any topological space $Z$ and $z\in Z$, $\pi_n(Z,z)$, $n\geq1$, consists of continuous maps $([0,1]^n,\partial[0,1]^n)\to(Z,z)$ modulo homotopy relative to the boundary, with concatenation in the first coordinate. Call a continuous map a weak homotopy equivalence when it induces a bijection on path components and an isomorphism on every $\pi_n$ at every source basepoint. Let $h:X\to Y$ be a continuous map of arbitrary topological spaces and let $U,V\subseteq Y$ be open subsets with $Y=U\cup V$. Give all subsets their subspace topologies. If the three restrictions $$h:h^{-1}(U)\to U,\qquad h:h^{-1}(V)\to V,\qquad h:h^{-1}(U\cap V)\to U\cap V$$ are weak homotopy equivalences, then $h:X\to Y$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. No separation, compact-generation or connectedness hypothesis is imposed, and empty spaces and empty intersections are allowed.
